about: Switch model number -> SoC / board codename -> where its drivers come from. 'status' says whether this repository can produce a driver set for the model. Nothing here claims a driver works on hardware.

HAC-001.name: Nintendo Switch (original, Erista / Tegra X1)
HAC-001.note: Built and test-signed by .github/workflows/build-all-drivers.yml (Windows runner with WDK); tools/build/assemble_build.py puts the result in build/HAC-001/drivers/. Not built in the authoring environment, no real-console test of the whole set.

HAC-001-01.name: Nintendo Switch (2019 revision, Mariko / Tegra X1+)
HAC-001-01.note: This repository has no driver set for Iowa (docs/DRIVER-INVENTORY.md: 'Iowa は専用の枠なし'). The Erista and Lite sets are NOT reused: board, power and I2C wiring are not shown to match.

HDH-001.name: Nintendo Switch Lite (Mariko / Tegra X1+)
HDH-001.note: Sources and INFs are present, but no CI build configuration exists yet (the Lite copy of Build-Driver.ps1 is older than the Erista one, and the per-driver build flags have not been written down).

HEG-001.name: Nintendo Switch OLED (Mariko / Tegra X1+)
HEG-001.note: The only reported-working OLED set is windows-switch v0.8.0 (one console, per its release note). Its source (swhid, swbatt, swagentsvc, shim, UEFI patches, scripts) is kept under drivers/t214-aula/drivers/<Driver>/ (swhid, swbatt, touchread, swagentsvc) and drivers/t214-aula/upstream-src/ but has NOT been built in this repository (needs the upstream Docker/mingw toolchain); the prebuilt binaries are the upstream ones. tools/build/fill_heg001.py takes YOUR copy of that release zip, checks every file against the SHA-256 in drivers/t214-aula/manifest/, and fills build/HEG-001/.
